page: Microsoft Azure E112ibs_v5 is an isolated virtual machine instance belonging to the EIBSv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 112 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 56 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz. The x86_64 architecture is supported by 48 KB L1d, 1 MB L2, and 48 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 672.0 GB of system memory, providing 6.0 GB of RAM per core. It contains no local storage and zero GPUs, but is designed with Premium Storage capability and optimized block storage performance.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core and memory performance. The instance achieved a strong rating in stress-ng multi-core CPU performance with a score of 108538.83 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 17915.0. Memory bandwidth is a notable strength, with read-only small block cached bandwidth reaching 5839.55 GB/sec and uncached large block read bandwidth at 335.8 GB/sec. Passmark CPU encryption tests placed the server in the top tier with a score of 94803.53, while database operations and Redis SET operations both demonstrated strong performance. Conversely, single-core metrics, such as stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core, remained in the average tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E112ibs_v5 offers high resource density with 112 dedicated vCPUs and 672.0 GB of RAM, making it suitable for workloads requiring substantial memory capacity without the overhead of local storage. The primary tradeoff is the complete absence of local NVMe storage, meaning all storage operations must rely on external block storage, though the instance is optimized for Premium Storage. Additionally, single-threaded performance is average, meaning workloads that cannot parallelize effectively will not fully exploit the hardware's capabilities.

This server configuration is suited for memory-intensive, highly parallelized workloads. Appropriate applications include large-scale database operations, Redis caching layers, multi-threaded software compilation, and static web serving. It is also capable of handling moderate LLM inference tasks for smaller models, though the lack of a GPU limits its utility for larger AI workloads.
